outline.section: H2: Fragrance-Free vs. Unscented: What the Labels Actually Mean
outline.guidance: This is a critical trust-building section that competitors handle poorly. Explain clearly: 'fragrance-free' means no fragrance ingredients added (synthetic or masking); 'unscented' often means masking agents were used to neutralize odor—and those masking agents can still be allergens. Cite the FDA or American Academy of Dermatology (AAD) on fragrance as a leading cause of contact dermatitis. Note that terms like 'naturally scented' or 'lightly scented' do not qualify as fragrance-free. This section should answer the question many Reddit users and sensitive-skin sufferers ask. Flag to writer: verify AAD or FDA source URL is live before linking.

outline.section: H2: What to Look For in a Truly Clean Fragrance-Free Lotion
outline.guidance: Briefly cover the ingredient criteria that define a genuinely clean fragrance-free lotion: (1) no synthetic fragrance or parfum on the label, (2) no essential oils used as fragrance (these are still allergens for many), (3) no masking agents, (4) free from parabens, phthalates, and sulfates, (5) key moisturizing actives present—such as glycerin, shea butter, aloe vera, or plant-based emollients. Mention that dermatologist-recommended formulas often prioritize these attributes. Do not name competitor brands. Position this as a buyer's checklist.
